ingredients: 6 chicken drumsticks with bone (450–500 g total; about 350 g meat once shredded)
1 tsp black pepper, plus a pinch for the chicken
method: Bring 1 litre of water to a boil in a saucepan.
Stir in the black pepper, salt to taste, and the slit green chillies.
Add the chicken drumsticks, cover, and simmer until cooked through, about 15 minutes.
Remove the drumsticks from the soup and shred the meat off the bone.
In a separate pan, melt the butter. Add the kasuri methi, a pinch of black pepper and salt, and the shredded chicken. Toss briefly, until the chicken is evenly coated.
Place the shredded chicken in the bottom of each bowl, then pour the hot soup over it. Serve immediately.
title: Pepper Chicken Soup
description: A high-protein, comforting chicken soup with a peppery broth and buttery, kasuri methi-coated chicken.

ingredients: 1 cup diced bell peppers and capsicum
1 small potato (added in the creator's recipe update)
method: Add all the soup-base ingredients to a pressure cooker and cook for 3 whistles.
After the pressure releases, remove the chicken thighs and shred the meat with a fork or shredder. Blend everything left in the cooker into a smooth purée.
Stir the shredded chicken back into the purée, then add the oregano and chilli flakes. Bring the soup to a boil.
Ladle into bowls while hot and finish with chopped parsley.
title: Creamy Chicken Soup (No Cream, No Oil)
description: A smooth, creamy-textured chicken soup with no cream or oil — the pressure-cooked vegetables are blended to give the broth its body.

method: Dry roast the pepper, garlic, and red chillies until fragrant. Transfer to a mortar and pestle and crush into a coarse mix. Keep aside.
In the same mortar and pestle, roughly crush the ginger, shallots, and tomato into a chunky mixture.
Heat the oil in a pressure cooker. Add the rasam spice mix and sauté for a few seconds, then add the tomato mixture and cook until fragrant. Add the turmeric and sauté until the raw smell disappears.

Pour in the water and let it come to a gentle simmer. Add the chicken, close the pressure cooker, and cook for about 4 whistles, or until the chicken is cooked through — be careful not to overcook so the chicken stays juicy.
Once done, remove the chicken and separate the meat from the bones. Serve the chicken with steamed rice and plenty of the warm, flavourful rasam broth.
title: Chicken Rasam Rice
description: Comfort in a bowl — bone-in chicken pressure-cooked in a tangy, spicy rasam broth with crushed pepper, garlic, shallots, and tomato, served over steamed rice.

method: Season the salmon fillet with the salt and black pepper.
Heat the olive oil over medium-high heat. Sear the salmon skin-side down for 2 minutes, then flip and cook for 2 minutes more.
Turn the heat to low. Peel off the crispy skin, break the salmon into pieces, then add the white onions, green onions, and garlic. Cook for about 1 minute, then scramble in the eggs.
Add the rice, soy sauce, oyster sauce, and sugar. Cook over high heat for 1–2 minutes, tossing everything together. Serve hot.
title: Salmon Fried Rice
description: A full-flavored salmon fried rice with crisp-seared fish, aromatics, eggs, and a savory soy-oyster sauce.

ingredients: Chicken thighs, bone-in and skinless, 500 g
Lime juice, from ½ lime (about 10 ml)
method: Heat the ghee in a pan over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds, cardamoms, cloves, cinnamon, mace, and bay leaves; sauté for about a minute until fragrant.
Add the sliced onion and sauté until golden brown (brown a little further for a deeper, sweeter, more savoury flavour).
Add the crushed garlic and ginger and mix well.
Add the chicken thighs, brown sugar, black pepper, and lime juice. Mix everything well.
Add the water followed by the washed basmati rice. Mix gently and bring to a consistent boil.
Cover with a lid, reduce the heat to low, and cook for 25 minutes.
Garnish with fresh coriander and serve.
title: Punjabi Pepper Chicken Pulao
description: A one-pot Punjabi-style pepper chicken pulao — whole spices bloomed in ghee, golden-brown onions, and bone-in chicken thighs layered with basmati rice and finished with fresh coriander.
source: Source: Instagram reel by @ral.livezy (Ralston D'Souza); recipe by @sunnybynite91

ingredients: Fresh coriander leaves, chopped, ¼ cup (est.)
method: Wash the basmati rice and soak it while you prepare the rest of the ingredients.
Chop the onions, ginger, garlic, and green chillies together; chop the coriander and mint leaves separately.
Poke the boiled eggs all over with a knife.
Cut the tomato into thick slices (no need to chop it).
Heat the oil in a wide pan and roast the cumin seeds.
Add the chopped onion, ginger, garlic, and chillies. Cook until golden brown.
Add the tomato slices and cook until they soften.
Add the whisked curd and stir well.
Add the turmeric powder, Kashmiri red chilli powder, biryani masala, and salt. Stir to cook the masala.
Add the chopped coriander and mint leaves, stir it well, and cook the masala until the oil separates.
Add the boiled eggs and mix so they are coated in the masala.
Add double the amount of water as the rice, then add the soaked rice and stir well.
Taste and adjust the salt.
Once it comes to a simmer, tie a cloth over the lid, place the lid on the pan, and cook on a low flame for 10–12 minutes.
Rest briefly, then fluff and serve hot.
title: Egg Pulao
description: A one-pot, minimum-effort egg pulao — khille khille rice layered with perfectly spiced masala-coated eggs, finished with a 10-minute dum.
source: Source: Instagram reel by @yourfoodlab (Chef Sanjyot Keer)

method: Clean the chicken breast pieces, then coat them well with all the marinade ingredients.
Refrigerate the marinated chicken for 5–6 hours, or overnight for a deeper flavor.
Brush a pan with a little oil and cook the chicken, turning so both sides cook through. The pieces should be juicy and tender inside and crisp and brown outside.
Whisk together the Greek yogurt, salt, pepper, lime juice, grated garlic, and chopped coriander to make the dip.
Serve the pan-fried chicken with the garlic yogurt dip.
title: Lemon Pepper Chicken with Garlic Yogurt Dip
description: Crispy-on-the-outside, juicy-on-the-inside chicken breast pieces marinated in lemon and pepper, served with a creamy garlic yogurt dip.

ingredients: 80 g Greek yogurt, divided (set aside 1 tbsp for blending)
method: Marinate the chicken breast with the ginger-garlic paste, cumin, coriander, cardamom, paprika, salt, and lemon juice. Let it rest, or grill it right away.
Lightly grease a pan with olive oil and grill the chicken until cooked through and charred on both sides.

Make the garlic sauce: blend the sesame seeds, olive oil, garlic cloves, 1 tablespoon of the Greek yogurt, lemon juice, and salt. Add the blended mixture to the remaining yogurt and whisk until smooth.
Slice the grilled chicken.
Arrange the lettuce, cucumber, onion, and cherry tomatoes in a bowl. Top with the sliced chicken, drizzle with the garlic sauce, and serve.
title: High-Protein Chicken Shawarma Salad
description: A 53g-protein, 360-calorie shawarma-style chicken salad — charred spice-marinated chicken over crisp vegetables with a creamy garlic-yogurt shawarma sauce.

ingredients: Chicken thighs, bone-in and skinless, 500 g
Chilli powder, 2 tsp (the creator used 1 tsp)
method: To a pan on medium heat, add the oil, ½ onion, tomato, dry red chillies, coriander, mint, cardamom, cumin seeds, peppercorns, and cloves. Mix well and cook for 5 minutes. Transfer everything to a blender and blend into a smooth paste. Set aside.
To the same pan on medium heat, add the oil and the finely chopped onion. Fry until the onions turn nice and golden brown. Add the ginger-garlic paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the coriander, mint leaves, and turmeric powder. Mix well.
Add the chicken thighs, chilli powder, and salt. Coat the chicken nicely with all the masala.
Cover and cook for 10 minutes so the chicken releases its water and starts to cook through.
Add the paste made earlier. Mix everything really well, cover again, and cook for another 5 minutes.
Add the coriander powder and shredded coconut. Give it a final mix and roast until nice and dry. Serve.
title: Sukha Chicken Roast
description: A dry-roasted chicken tossed in a freshly ground onion-tomato-spice paste with coriander and mint, finished with shredded coconut and roasted until dry.
source: Source: Instagram reel by @ral.livezy (Ralston D'Souza); recipe by @terrace_village_kitchen

ingredients: Ching's Secret Green Chilli Sauce, 3–4 tbsp (est.)
method: Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Add the finely chopped onion and sauté until soft and lightly golden.
Add the chopped garlic and ginger and sauté for a minute until fragrant.
Add the slit green chillies and the boneless chicken pieces. Sprinkle over the salt and toss well.
Spoon in the coriander powder and garam masala, mix to coat the chicken evenly, and cook, tossing occasionally, until the chicken is cooked through and lightly browned.
Toss in the chopped coriander leaves and mix through.
Pour the green chilli sauce over the chicken and toss everything until the pieces are glossy and well glazed.
Serve hot, straight from the pan.
title: Green Chicken Chilli
description: A one-pan, beginner-friendly desi-style chicken chilli — boneless chicken sautéed with onion, lots of garlic and ginger, and slit green chillies, finished with a generous pour of green chilli sauce.

ingredients: Coriander leaves, chopped, a few sprigs
method: Heat the ghee in a pan. Add the garlic cloves along with the green chillies and sauté.
Add the chicken and cook for 2 minutes on high heat.
Season with salt and crushed pepper, mix well, then cover and cook for 12–15 minutes, opening and stirring in between to prevent the chicken from burning.
Once the chicken is cooked, finish with the chopped coriander leaves.
Serve hot.
title: Simple Ghee-Garlic Chicken
description: A classic example of simple ingredients tasting fantastic — chicken cooked in ghee with garlic, green chillies, and crushed pepper until tender.

method: Add the peeled shallots, garlic cloves, red chilli powder, turmeric, and salt to a mixer jar and blend into a thick paste.
Heat the oil in a pan. Add the cumin seeds and let them splutter.
Add the blended paste and fry it for several minutes, stirring, until it cooks down.
Add the chopped onion and curry leaves and keep stirring until the mixture is dry and oil glistens at the edges.
Mix the hot pachadi into cooked white rice by hand until evenly coated orange-red. Serve and eat hot.
title: Onion Vellulli Pachadi (Onion-Garlic Chutney with Rice)
description: A spicy Telugu-style onion-garlic pachadi — shallots, garlic, red chilli and turmeric blended into a paste, fried in oil with cumin, onion and curry leaves, then mixed by hand with hot white rice. Deep red, oily, and eaten as a full rice meal.

ingredients: Salt, 1 tsp (for boiling) + 1 tsp (for the masala)
Turmeric powder, ½ tsp (for boiling) + ½ tsp (for the masala)
method: Boil the soya chunks in water with 1 tsp salt and ½ tsp turmeric powder for 5 minutes, then drain the water out.
Heat ½ tbsp oil with 1 tsp butter in a pan over medium heat. Sauté the boiled, drained soya chunks for about 5 minutes until lightly golden brown, then set aside.
To the same pan add ½ tbsp oil and 1 tsp butter. Sauté the onion until nice and golden brown.
Add the ginger-garlic paste, slit green chilli, and tomato. Cook until the tomato turns nice and mushy.
Add the Kashmiri red chilli powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, turmeric powder, and pepper powder. Mix everything well.
Add the salt, cashew paste, and yogurt. Mix well, then add the cooked soya chunks and coat them nicely with the masala.
Add the water, mix well, cover, and cook for 10 minutes.
Finish with the garam masala, kasuri methi, butter, and fresh coriander. Give it one final mix and serve.
title: Restaurant Style Soya Masala
description: A restaurant-style soya masala — turmeric-boiled soya chunks crisped in butter, folded into a rich onion-tomato-cashew masala and finished with garam masala and kasuri methi.
source: Source: Instagram reel by @ral.livezy (Ralston D'Souza); recipe by @sekhiya.kitchen

ingredients: Thick white paste — appears to be curd (yogurt) (est.)
method: In a bowl, combine the oil, red chilli powder, coriander powder, chopped green chillies, fried onion, and the thick white paste. Add salt and mix into a thick marinade.
Add the chicken pieces to the marinade and mix well, coating each piece.
Transfer the marinated chicken to a hot pan or kadai.
Pour in water and add the extra red chilli powder. Stir well.
Cook, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is cooked through and the gravy thickens to a rich, glossy curry.
Drizzle ghee over the simmering curry and give it a final stir.
Garnish with fresh coriander and serve hot with an onion salad and a lime wedge.
title: Nizami Chicken
description: A rich, creamy, spicy Nizami-style chicken curry — chicken pieces marinated with fried onion, green chillies, and spices, simmered until thick and finished with ghee.
source: Source: Instagram reel by @themadchefindia (Chef Koushik S., The Mad Chef India) — reconstructed from the video's on-screen labels; all quantities estimated

ingredients: Spinach, blanched, 2 packed cups raw (70 g)
Fresh coriander, packed, ½ cup (15 g)
Tomato puree, ¼ cup (60 g) + a splash of water
method: Blend the paneer, blanched spinach, coriander, mint, green chillies, and a little water into a smooth, creamy, vibrant green paste. Set aside.
Heat the oil in a pan and add the bay leaf, cinnamon, cloves, and cardamom. Let them crackle.
Add the onion and ginger-garlic paste and sauté until golden brown.
Add the chilli powder, turmeric, coriander powder, and garam masala, then the tomato puree with a little water. Cook it out until the oil separates.

Lower the flame and stir in the green paneer puree. Keep the heat low and cook, stirring continuously, for 2 to 3 minutes (this stops it splitting and dulling in colour), then season with salt and sugar to taste.
Gently fold in the sliced boiled eggs and mix well.
For the tadka, heat the ghee and sizzle the chopped garlic with the Kashmiri chilli powder, then pour it over the curry. Finish with a sprinkle of coriander leaves.
title: Afghani Palak Paneer Egg Curry
description: Imagine crossing lasooni palak paneer with a creamy, zesty Afghani gravy — one pan, creamy, comforting, and way higher in protein.

ingredients: Onion, 1 medium to large, finely chopped
Maggi Masala Magic, ½ to 1 packet (to spice preference)
Fresh coriander leaves, a handful, chopped
method: Bring plenty of water to a rolling boil. Add a little oil and the two noodle cakes; cook 2–3 minutes until just done (a noodle should cut easily with a spoon).
Drain the noodles and spread them out on a large plate so they don't stick together.
Heat some butter in a pan. Add the chopped garlic and green chilli and sauté until fragrant.
Add the chopped onion and cook until softened.
Add both tastemaker packets, the salt, and the Masala Magic (½–1 packet depending on spice preference). Mix well.
Pour in 2–3 tablespoons of water and mix until the masala thickens and the water almost evaporates.
Add the soy sauce and mix again.
Gently add the boiled noodles and toss everything together with two forks or tongs, taking care not to break the noodles.
Finish with the lemon juice, fresh coriander, and a little extra butter. Mix gently and serve hot.
title: Lemon Coriander Maggi
description: The "bestestest" Maggi — butter-sautéed garlic, chilli, and onion tossed with noodles in a soy-maggi masala, finished with fresh lemon juice and coriander.
